name: East Venezuela Basin
note: Orinoco extra-heavy oil belt, charged by Querecual and San Antonio (Cenomanian-Santonian); the 2000 assessment covered conventional oil only, so the USGS figure of 30 billion barrels omits the belt

name: Mesopotamian Foredeep Basin
note: Sargelu and Naokelekan (Jurassic) with Garau and Sulaiy (Cretaceous); raised toward Iraqi and Kuwaiti reserves plus cumulative production

name: Greater Ghawar Uplift
note: Hanifa and Tuwaiq Mountain (Upper Jurassic) charge Ghawar; note this is a different source rock from the Silurian that charges the gas

name: Zagros Fold Belt
note: Kazhdumi (Albian) and Garau for Iranian oil; Pabdeh (Paleogene) in other; raised toward Iranian reserves plus cumulative

name: Alberta Basin
note: Athabasca and Peace River oil sands, charged from Exshaw and Duvernay (Devonian-Mississippian) and Nordegg (Lower Jurassic, in other); oil sands are excluded from the conventional assessment

name: West Siberian Basin
note: Bazhenov (Tithonian) is the oil source, unlike the Cenomanian Pokur that charges the gas

name: Rub Al Khali Basin
note: Upper Jurassic with Shuaiba and other Cretaceous sources; raised toward Emirati and Saudi reserves

name: Maracaibo Basin
note: La Luna (Cenomanian-Campanian); raised for cumulative production, which is large and old

name: Niger Delta
note: Akata and Agbada; raised toward Nigerian reserves plus cumulative

name: Sirte Basin
note: Sirte Shale (Campanian) in other; Rachmat and Etel (Turonian) in mid-Cretaceous; raised toward Libyan reserves

name: North Sea Graben
note: Kimmeridge Clay and Draupne; no Carboniferous contribution to oil, unlike the gas

name: Permian Basin
note: Wolfcamp, Bone Spring and Spraberry (Permian); Woodford secondary; US not covered by the 2000 world assessment

name: North Caspian Basin
note: Tengiz, Kashagan and Karachaganak; Domanik-type Devonian-Carboniferous sources

name: Western Gulf
note: Eagle Ford oil window (Cenomanian-Turonian); Gulf Coast Tertiary; Smackover secondary

name: Santos Basin
note: Pre-salt Lula and Buzios, Barremian-Aptian lacustrine source; discovered after 2006 so absent from the assessment

name: Bohaiwan Basin
note: Shahejie (Eocene-Oligocene) lacustrine; Daqing area excluded, see Songliao

name: Northern Alaska
note: Shublik (Triassic) in other; HRZ and pebble shale (Cretaceous); Prudhoe Bay

name: Widyan Basin-Int. Platform
note: Upper Jurassic with a Silurian contribution

name: Guyana-Suriname Basin
note: Stabroek block, Canje Formation (Cenomanian-Turonian); discovered 2015, absent from the assessment

name: Trias/Ghadames Basin
note: Frasnian (Devonian) dominant for oil; Silurian Tanezzuft secondary

name: West-central Coastal
note: Bucomazi (Barremian lacustrine) and Cenomanian-Turonian marine; Congo and Gabon

name: Williston Basin
note: Bakken and Three Forks (Devonian-Mississippian), US portion

name: Los Angeles Basin
note: Monterey (Miocene); among the most prolific basins per unit area on Earth

name: East Texas Basin
note: Smackover and Bossier; Eagle Ford and Woodbine

name: Bend Arch-Fort Worth Basin
note: Barnett oil window and Pennsylvanian sources

name: Appalachian Basin
note: Devonian black shales; Ordovician in other

name: Gippsland Basin
note: Latrobe Group, Late Cretaceous to Eocene

name: Uinta-Piceance Basins
note: Green River Formation (Eocene lacustrine) in other; Mancos secondary

name: Big Horn Basin
note: Mowry and Cody; Phosphoria (Permian) and Devonian secondary

name: Neuquen Basin
note: Vaca Muerta (Tithonian); Los Molles in other

name: Northwest German Basin
note: Posidonia Shale (Lower Jurassic, Toarcian) in other; Wealden secondary. The gas here comes from Carboniferous coal instead

name: Michigan Basin
note: Niagaran (Silurian) pinnacle reefs and Antrim-related Devonian sources

name: Qatar Arch
note: Upper Jurassic for the small oil leg; the giant gas accumulation here is Silurian-sourced

name: Amu-Darya Basin
note: Upper Jurassic; overwhelmingly a gas province

name: Ordos Basin
note: Yanchang Formation (Triassic lacustrine) in other; the gas here is Carboniferous-Permian instead

name: Anglo-Dutch Basin
note: Posidonia and Lias (Lower Jurassic); the gas here is Westphalian coal instead

name: Po Basin
note: Triassic sources in other; Miocene-Pliocene secondary

name: Sichuan Basin
note: Triassic and older sources; a gas province, not an oil one
